findings.title: Irreversible data loss: table dropped with no archive, guard, or downgrade
findings.evidence: The added statement is 'conn.execute("DROP TABLE legacy_users")' executed inside upgrade() with no preceding copy/archive of rows, no emptiness check, and no corresponding restore step visible in the hunk.
findings.recommendation: Reachability: running upgrade() against any database where legacy_users still holds rows deletes them permanently. Before dropping, archive the rows (e.g. CREATE TABLE legacy_users_archive AS SELECT * or export) or assert the table is empty and abort otherwise; add/verify an explicit downgrade() that recreates the table so the migration is reversible.

findings.title: No IF EXISTS: migration hard-fails and leaves schema half-migrated
findings.evidence: The added line 'conn.execute("DROP TABLE legacy_users")' uses a bare DROP TABLE with no IF EXISTS or prior existence probe, and it is sequenced after 'conn.execute("DROP INDEX idx_legacy_email")'.
findings.recommendation: Reachability: on a fresh database or one where the table was never created / was already removed, upgrade() raises an error after the index was already dropped, so the environment is left with the index gone and no way to re-run cleanly. Use 'DROP TABLE IF EXISTS legacy_users' (or query the catalog first) so the step is idempotent, and keep the destructive steps ordered/atomic so partial application cannot strand the schema.

findings.title: Destructive migration added with no test exercising the drop or its absence case
findings.evidence: No test commands were run for this change, and the added 'conn.execute("DROP TABLE legacy_users")' has no accompanying test for the table-absent and table-populated paths.
findings.recommendation: Add migration tests covering (a) upgrade() on a DB where legacy_users does not exist, (b) upgrade() where it exists with rows (assert archived/empty-guard behaviour), and (c) FK dependencies, since DROP TABLE without CASCADE fails on PostgreSQL when other objects reference the table.
